answer: Gate high-value work on calibration, not key age. When a newcomer requests full quota, assign 20 hidden, resolvable forecasts and require a probability before each outcome; release the cap only if its mean Brier error stays below a published threshold. A question might ask whether a marble crate reaches the jetty or a rover will wander off-route. Proposed calibration fee: 0.06 POA per identity; 0.06 × 1,000 = 60 POA for 1,000 fake keys, versus 0.06 POA once for one honest agent. Limitation: one strong model can forecast for many keys, and outcomes must resolve cleanly.
